blocks.text: The lattice energy of a compound cannot be determined by a single direct experiment, but it can be calculated from several experimental data using an energy cycle called the Born-Haber cycle, an application of Hess's law. For sodium chloride the elements Na(s) + 1/2 Cl2(g) form the solid NaCl directly (delta Hf, the standard enthalpy of formation, measured conveniently in a calorimeter) or go through the gaseous ions Na+(g) + Cl-(g): delta Hx is the total energy involved in changing sodium and chlorine from their standard states to gaseous ions, and the gaseous ions then form the solid (delta Hlatt). By Hess's law delta Hx + delta Hlatt = delta Hf. The energy triangle extended to show the stages of delta Hx is the complete Born-Haber cycle.

blocks.alt: An enthalpy ladder: from sodium metal and chlorine gas, green arrows climb through atomization of sodium (+108), atomization of chlorine (+121) and ionization of sodium (+496) to sodium ions, electrons and chlorine atoms; a red arrow drops by the electron affinity (-349) to the gaseous ions, and a long red arrow falls to solid NaCl by the lattice energy; a blue arrow for the enthalpy of formation (-411) joins the start to the end. Boxes at the right work the sums and define each term.
blocks.caption: The Born-Haber cycle of sodium chloride with the printed values (original diagram after Figures 6.8 and 6.9; not to scale).
blocks.long_description: Starting from the elements, sodium is atomized and ionized and chlorine is atomized, all endothermic, then chlorine atoms gain electrons, exothermic; these four steps add to delta Hx = +376 kJ per mol. The direct route is the enthalpy of formation, -411. Since the two routes meet at solid NaCl, the lattice energy is -411 - 376 = -787 kJ per mol, a value no single experiment could give.

blocks.caption: Born-Haber cycle of NaCl (Figure 6.9), kJ per mol
rows: Lattice energy = delta Hf - delta Hx

blocks.text: Sample Problem 6.9: the heat of formation of sodium fluoride, which crystallizes in the sodium chloride lattice, from its cycle. The heat of atomization of Na(s) is 109, half the bond energy of F2 is 79, the ionization energy of sodium is 494, the electron affinity of fluorine is -328 and the lattice energy is -939 kJ per mol: delta Hf = -939 + 109 + 494 + 79 - 328 = -585 kJ per mol.

blocks.prompt: Calculate the heat of formation of lithium fluoride: atomization of Li(s) 161, half the F2 bond energy 79, ionization of lithium 520, electron affinity of fluorine -328, lattice energy -1107 kJ per mol (printed without its sign).
blocks.explanation: Delta Hf = delta Hlatt + delta Hat(Li) + IE(Li) + delta Hat(F) + EA(F) = -1107 + 161 + 520 + 79 - 328 = -675 kJ per mol.

items: Born-Haber cycle: Hess's law applied to an ionic solid; delta Hx (atomizations + ionization + electron affinity) + delta Hlatt = delta Hf. NaCl: 108 + 496 + 121 - 349 = +376; lattice energy = -411 - 376 = -787 kJ per mol. NaF formation: -939 + 109 + 494 + 79 - 328 = -585 kJ per mol.
